title: Controller state model registration
description: What a controller tells the hub about itself, once, so the hub can prepare a sync contract for it. The registration is the controller's live state model: the composite documents it writes, the primitives they decompose to, the state machine it exposes, the dosing inputs it can supply, and the settings it will publish. Everything the hub offers back - the cursor, the batch endpoints, the allowed filters - is derived from this, so a controller never negotiates a query shape at request time.

versionRange.description: Builds this registration describes. A registration is versioned because algorithm behaviour changes between releases, which is why a decision without a version cannot be reproduced.

source.description: Where this registration was derived from.

cadence.description: How often the controller expects to sync. The hub uses it to size pages and to tell a replay consumer what a gap means.

maxDeferralSeconds.description: How long the controller may batch before it must flush. Bounds how stale a follower can be.

documents.description: The composite wire documents this controller writes. Composite on the wire keeps the edge device's request count down; the hub decomposes for storage and query.

discriminator.description: How the hub recognises this controller's documents in a shared collection - a devicestatus carrying a `loop` object rather than an `openaps` one. Deliberately structural, never the free-text device string.

decomposesTo.description: Primitive record types the hub will produce. Named so decomposition coverage is a contract rather than a surprise.

paths.description: Dotted wire paths this controller writes in this collection.

stateSpans.description: The state machine this controller exposes, as time-ranged spans rather than point events. Categories the hub can render, query and reconcile across sources.

supersedes.description: Whether a later span from this controller supersedes an overlapping one, which is how two controllers or a human and a controller are reconciled.

replayInputs.description: The dosing inputs this controller can supply, and where. An input declared with a null path is declared-and-unrecorded: the honest statement that the controller has the value and does not publish it. That is what makes replay completeness measurable instead of guessed.

settings.description: The configuration snapshot this controller will publish. Versioned and effective-dated, because a setting that changed mid-history invalidates a replay that assumed one value.

queryProfile.description: What the hub will let this controller ask for. Derived from the registration rather than negotiated per request, which is how query cost stays bounded: there is no operator here that can reach storage without an index.
